selection.rationale: Single-device task (resources.json: communication not_applicable), so the only lever for latency_ms is the timed run() itself. Measured facts: the project group 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb (call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0) is the complete batch=1 FP32 forward; coverage shows 81 CUDA kernels all associated to this root, with 724.4us nested diagnostic CUDA under intrusive hooks versus the immutable 1.631ms clean original baseline and 3.924ms perturbed profiled wall, so kernel time alone does not bound wall latency and launch/dispatch overhead in the whole-run plan is the plausible remaining cost. Within this timed boundary the only editable non-hook subordinate call is the aten::clone of the (1,1000) FP32 logits (call ff665ce97a6a868dae8ae228, group 25f0b0f6ce52aabeb54e), which materializes the installed CUDA-graph plan's output each replay; it and the whole-run wrapper need one another (changing output handling requires recapturing/rewiring the plan), so they form one joint execution-plan boundary, matching the installed bundle trial-68d4b40978-param-34913d45 that already owns exactly these two calls. The record_function enter/exit groups (d9e5d004d6d24251774f, 4bc9b83f44937f869781, 798df708d05932b17f71) are discovery hooks with zero CUDA time, not project work, and are excluded. The previous round's failure was a missing discovery.json during search (infrastructure), not a measured quality or performance rejection; no previous-candidate manifest exists, and this selection is made against the current re-collected discovery, retaining the installed graph+BN-fold plan as the accepted base to extend or replace.
selection.hypothesis: A revised whole-run execution plan at the same boundary can reduce measured latency_ms below the current installed plan by removing per-replay dispatch overhead that remains between the ~0.72ms hook-perturbed kernel time and the clean wall time: concretely, folding the logits materialization into the captured graph (or otherwise eliminating the separate clone launch after replay) and further trimming launch count/gaps inside the replayed plan while keeping FP32, TF32 disabled, cudnn.benchmark False, the frozen first-image fixture, and NCHW policies unchanged. Expected benefit is a hypothesis to be tested: acceptance requires independently measured latency_ms improvement with all logits within atol=rtol=1e-4 and exact top-1 equality; if the clone-in-graph or replay trimming breaks fidelity, the plan must fall back to the installed strategy rather than the eager reference.

proposal.rationale: Previous feedback: the prior round failed with FileNotFoundError on discovery.json inside the search harness (infrastructure), not a measured quality or performance rejection, and no previous-candidate manifest exists; so this attempt extends the accepted installed base (trial-68d4b40978-param-34913d45: BN-fold + whole-run NCHW CUDA graph, which it explicitly replaces and fully re-implements, including its generic hook-discovered fold as the last fallback) instead of repairing a rejected candidate. Measured facts from target-resources.json: the replayed plan still launches 81 CUDA kernels per project.invoke, and roughly 48 of them are small elementwise kernels - one folded-bias CUDAFunctor_add after every convolution and one launch_clamp_scalar ReLU per activation site, plus a separate 3-arg residual add per block - while the convolutions themselves are winograd/implicit_convolve_sgemm kernels chosen by the cudnn heuristic with benchmark disabled. The remaining latency lever inside this frozen boundary is therefore the composition of the replayed plan itself, not per-op dispatch (replay launch cost is already graph-amortized and the wrapper's CPU work is hidden under ~0.7ms+ of GPU time). This candidate keeps the installed boundary, policies (FP32, TF32 disabled, cudnn.benchmark False, NCHW, frozen fixture, seed) and lifecycle, but slims the replay: (a) eval BN stays folded into conv weights/biases; (b) shortcut 1x1 convolutions run bias-free with their folded bias merged into the following convolution's bias (exact linear merge); (c) at build time, on the leased worker GPU, each site's conv+bias+ReLU (aten::cudnn_convolution_relu) and conv+bias+residual-add+ReLU (aten::cudnn_convolution_add_relu, alpha=1) fused epilogues are timed against the unfused chain on the real captured activations, and adopted per site only when faster; (d) the resulting whole-run graph is accepted only if its measured replay time beats the all-unfused (installed-equivalent) graph by more than 2%. Numerical safety is enforced at build time before anything can be used: fused-op semantic probes (vs F.conv2d+relu compositions at 1e-5, which also rejects any silent TF32 divergence), then patched-eager logits, replay-vs-patched-eager at 1e-5, and both vs the pristine original model's logits at the frozen quality tolerance 1e-4 with exact top-1 equality; any failure falls back down the ladder fused -> installed-equivalent unfused graph -> generic installed-bundle fold+graph -> parent adapter.run, so the worst case is the installed plan's behavior, never silent numerics drift. The per-replay aten::clone of the (1,1000) logits (call ff665ce97a6a868dae8ae228) is deliberately retained inside the boundary to preserve adapter.run's fresh-output alias semantics (each invocation returns a distinct tensor) rather than returning graph-owned static memory; its launch overlaps the replay on the CPU side. The workload executes on every invocation: replay recomputes all kernels from the live static input buffer, and a different same-signature pixels tensor is copied into it and recomputed (no fixture-dependent outputs are cached). record_route reports the actually chosen path (graph-convbiasrelu / graph-foldbn / graph-foldbn-generic / parent-fallback) from inside the replacement.

steps: One pristine eager forward of the untouched model to freeze reference logits for all later verifications.

GPU micro-probes of aten::cudnn_convolution_relu and aten::cudnn_convolution_add_relu (small 3x3 s1 and s2 shapes) against F.conv2d-based references at atol=rtol=1e-5; failure disables the fused path entirely.
All-unfused patch applied once (BN fold into convs, shortcut folded bias merged into the next conv bias) and one hooked forward captures each basic block's real input activation.
Per-site timing (30 warm-synced reps per variant) of fused vs unfused chains for the stem and each block's conv1 and conv2 on the captured activations; patch restored afterwards.

Candidate plan graphs captured (3 side-stream warmup iters, torch.cuda.CUDAGraph capture), replay-verified and replay-timed (45 reps, median); the loser graph is reset and its pool released, the winner's patch is re-applied with the identical Parameter objects the winning graph was captured against, followed by one final eager verification against the reference logits.
Total build GPU work is bounded (tens of forward-scale operations plus ~90 graph replays, well under the worker timeout).
memory: Folded conv weights/biases are new FP32 Parameter tensors; the original conv Parameters stay referenced by the plan's restore records for the process lifetime, so standing allocated memory grows by roughly the conv weight footprint (11,166,912 params x 4 B ~= 44.7 MB), same in kind as the installed bundle it replaces.

Two CUDA graph private pools are captured transiently during build; the loser's pool is released via graph reset and only the winner's pool is retained for the process lifetime (raises reserved memory; per-run framework.peak_allocated_bytes is unaffected by the pool itself but includes the standing folded-weight allocations described above).
Per graph: one static input buffer (1x3x224x224 FP32 = 602,112 B) and static logits (4,000 B); the loser's buffers are freed when its plan is dropped.
Build-time site-activation capture temporarily holds the 8 block inputs (~4 MB) and is released after variant selection.

quality_risks: Fused epilogue ops may select different cudnn convolution algorithms (e.g. implicit GEMM with epilogue instead of winograd), changing FP32 accumulation order; every stage is verified against the pristine eager model at the frozen atol=rtol=1e-4 with exact top-1 equality at build time, and any mismatch falls back to the installed-equivalent unfused plan before the candidate can be installed.

aten::cudnn_convolution_relu/add_relu take no explicit allow_tf32 flag; the build-time probes and full-plan verifications compare against FP32 eager references with TF32 disabled, so any TF32-internal divergence would be rejected rather than shipped.
The fused-op residual semantics relu(conv(x,w,b) + z) with alpha=1 is probed directly on the worker GPU before any use; if it differs, conv2 sites keep the unfused chain.

Build-time per-site timing noise could pick a marginally slower variant; the whole-graph adoption margin (fused only if >=2% faster than the installed-equivalent graph) biases every ambiguous case back to the installed behavior.

Model state stays patched (folded weights plus custom site forwards) after build for the winner, so the wrapper's parent-fallback path also runs through the verified patched model; this state is verified twice against the original eager logits (plan build and post-selection) and restore machinery exists, but the runtime model is not bit-identical to the pretrained state - it is equivalence-verified to 1e-4/top-1 only.

If every plan level fails (e.g. capture unavailable), build returns an empty mapping and the unmodified parent adapter.run serves the workload at the pre-graph baseline; correctness is never traded for the plan.
